Base isolation table in reverse. The table top "floats" on a set of dampers which absorb energy and prevent it from being transferred to the base. In seismic systems we employ the same principle to prevent or reduce a foundation taking seismic load from the ground. In this case the input is applied by the metronomes to the tabletop so the tabletop just moves back and forth with little energy loss. Metronome input is all harmonic, so eventually they sync up because of conservation as the momentum of the masses working against each other eventually cause their own damping effect.
